title: Counterparty risk walkthrough & negotiation notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal walkthrough to log key clause flags, fallback language, and sales-facing talking points for counterparty X (SaaS reseller). Not a final legal position — use for calls and quick redlines.

Topline summary (one-liner): counterparty pushing broad liability + audit + data use; high priority to protect unit economics and IP. Push back required on indemnity scope, data ownership, and unlimited audit timeframe.

Immediate redline watchlist (ordered by severity):
- Liability cap: proposed unlimited or >12 months of fees. RED FLAG. Aim for aggregate cap = lesser of (12 months fees) or $X (for pilot set to $50k).
- Indemnity: asking for third-party claims + product misuse broad clause. Narrow to direct claims arising from breach/neglect. Exclude downstream customer claims where Redwood complied with spec.
- Data ownership & use: they want right to use outputs for model training. NO. We must limit to performance/improvement analytics only with strict de-identification and opt-out.
- Confidentiality carve-outs: they requested product output be outside NDA. Keep outputs confidential if they are derived from customer data or contain PII.
- Security audit & access: unlimited on-prem audits and right to copy logs. Propose scheduled SOC2/ISO proof or controlled audit with scope and notice.
- Termination for convenience: they want 30-day exit with full refund; accept 60–90 days notice and prorated refunds only; require transition assistance fees.
- Escrow/IP assignment: they propose broad assignment on insolvency — limit to narrow, time-bound obligations; do not assign core IP.
- Subprocessors/subcontracting: require notice and ability to object for high-risk subprocessors (e.g., cloud region changes).
- Warranty period & SLA credits: they want strict liquidated damages; convert to service credits and cap.
- Data breach notification timelines: they asked for 24h notification. Target 48–72h with initial acknowledgement within 24h.

Suggested redline snippets (quick paste candidates):
- Liability cap: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Redwood arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the lesser of (i) twelve (12) months of Fees paid by Customer under this Agreement; or (ii) $50,000. The foregoing limitation shall not apply to liability resulting from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence."
- Indemnity narrow: "Each party shall indemnify the other for Third Party Claims solely to the extent such Claims arise from the indemnifying party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of representations and warranties in this Agreement."
- Data use: "Customer Data and Customer Outputs shall remain the property of Customer. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement and diagnostics only; Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or improve models that are made available to third parties without Customer's prior written consent."
- Audit scope control: "Customer may request an audit no more than once per 12 months, subject to reasonable notice (30 days), and shall bear reasonable costs unless the audit reveals a material non-compliance."

Negotiation playbook / talking points for AE before first redline:
- Emphasize product value (predictable latency, cost savings via batching) not just price; we can offer short pilot with limited access to production models.
- For liability caps: contextualize with low per-customer spend — unlimited liability kills viability. Offer escrow + enhanced SLA for an enterprise commit.
- For data training asks: propose data usage pilot (time-limited, explicit opt-in) with strong DP/aggregation guarantees — or paid advanced analytics add-on.
- On audits: offer SOC2 reports and customer-specific assessments performed by vetted third party; we avoid unlimited on-site inspection for security reasons.

Fallback compromise ladder (best -> acceptable -> walk):
- Best: Full carveouts protecting outputs + 12-month fee cap + restricted indemnity + 48h breach notification + controlled audit process.
- Acceptable: 18-month fee cap + narrowly tailored indemnity with exclusions for model outputs + SOC2 + one paid audit per year.
- Walk: Unlimited liability, rights to use outputs for training, or unlimited audits. Escalate immediately to Legal Director if negotiation moves here.

Operational / finance considerations:
- If they insist on higher liability cap, require insurance certificate (cyber/GL) and add premium.
- Any data training opt-in should be a paid add-on; capture in SOW and list the datasets, retention, and deletion schedule.
- Transition assistance: define hourly rate and minimum notice to avoid churn cost.

Questions to ask counsel (to resolve before final sign):
- Is there a clean precedent clause we can reuse for "outputs not for model training"? (send Confluence link).
- How to phrase insolvency assignment carveout to avoid unintentionally transferring core IP?
- Confirm acceptable SLA credit calculation method that legal is comfortable defending.

Notes to self / call prep bullets:
- Bring example redlines from CONFLUENCE-1234 and JIRA-9876.
- Tell AE: if counterparty insists on training rights, get a signed RACI and budget for a paid data-sharing engagement.
- Keep negotiation tone collaborative: we want them as reference customers but can't accept open-ended obligations.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Draft redline with proposed snippets above (owner: Asha) — 48 hours.
- Loop in Nora for data-use language review (owner: Nora) — 24 hours.
- If they push audit clause, request SOC2 + auditor name first (owner: Liam) — ASAP.

Slack links / refs: #legal-contracts, #sales-enterprise, thread: slack.com/archives/C1234-aws-negotiation (add link to call notes after).

Quick heuristics: if counterparty asks for: "use for training" = ask for money/consent; "unlimited audits" = require SOC2 or paid audit; "low cap" = offer higher cap but with insurance.

Open uncertainties / flags to resolve:
- Proposed $ cap amount for pilot vs enterprise: decide with finance. Current placeholder $50k for pilots.
- Export controls language when they operate in EU + APAC: coordinate with compliance.

—— end of scratchpad.

(Do not treat this as final; file to be copied into shared_drives/legal once cleaned.)
